grows/grow: Nothing in the store is ever changed, and nothing leaves on its own. Every build adds folders.
grows/upgrade: Upgrade curl, and the new curl gets a new folder. The old one is still there.
grows/count: Keep going, and it adds up. This machine has over six thousand paths.
grows/danger: But you cannot delete a folder because it looks old. Something may still point at it.
roots/promise: So Nix starts from a list of what must stay. Each entry on it is a garbage collector root, or G C root for short.
roots/result: Build something, and Nix leaves a link called result in your folder. That link is a root.
roots/profile: A profile is the set of programs you have installed. Each time it changes, Nix keeps the old set as a numbered generation, and every generation is a root.
roots/gcroots: The third kind is any link under slash nix slash var slash nix slash G C roots. Add one there, and you have made a root by hand.
roots/query: Query roots tells you what is holding a path. Here, OpenSSL is held by a result link and by a generation.
live/walk: To find what stays, start at each root and take its closure. Everything those walks reach is called live.
live/list: You already have the tool. Query requisites prints the closure of one root.
live/rest: Whatever no walk reached is garbage. Here, that is the old curl and the old OpenSSL.
live/safe: Deleting garbage is safe, and you already know why. A closure is complete: nothing inside it points outside it. So nothing live can point at garbage.
collect/held: Now say your previous generation still lists the old curl. A generation is a root, so the old curl is live.
collect/gc: nix store dash dash G C deletes whatever is not live. With that root in place, the old curl stays.
collect/d: nix collect garbage dash D first deletes your old generations. That takes the roots away.
collect/cost: Then it collects, and the old curl is gone. You get the space back, and you can no longer go back to those generations.
